subject: Learning Methods
title: Elaborative Interrogation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Elaborative Interrogation usable.

hook.text: Simply asking 'why is this true?' after learning a fact boosts retention by 30 to 50 percent in most studies.

buildup.text: Elaborative interrogation means generating explanations for stated facts rather than accepting them at face value.

discovery.text: The why question forces you to link new facts to existing knowledge, creating richer retrieval pathways.

twist.text: It works best when you have some background knowledge. Complete beginners may struggle to generate useful explanations.

climax.text: As you read, flag each key claim and ask: why would this be true? The answer cements it into long-term memory.

punchline.text: One word transforms learning. Ask why. Every time.

quiz.question: How does elaborative interrogation improve retention?
options: It forces you to re-read the material more carefully
Asking why links new facts to existing knowledge, creating richer retrieval paths
Questioning activates the brain's doubt center
